title: Condensed coefficient rings $\underline T$
statement:
The *pro-étale site of a point*, $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$, is the category of profinite sets
with the coherent topology. In it, a finite family $\{S_i\to S\}$ covers $S$ exactly when
$\coprod_iS_i\to S$ is surjective, and a sieve covers when it contains such a family. A
*condensed ring* is a sheaf of rings on $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object],
its underlying condensed abelian group is a ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$.

For a topological ring $T$, the condensed ring $\underline T$ is defined by its sections,

$$
\underline T(S):=C(S,T),
$$

with restriction by precomposition and pointwise ring operations. It is a sheaf, and its
underlying ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is commutative when $T$ is. A
continuous ring homomorphism $\varphi\colon T\to T'$ induces a morphism of condensed rings
$\varphi_*\colon\underline T\to\underline{T'}$ by postcomposition, and this is functorial in
$\varphi$.

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the absolute
value extending that of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. This gives the following commutative condensed
rings:

- $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ and $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, for the $\ell$-adic topologies;
- for a subfield $E$ of $\Qlb$ (a field with an embedding $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$), the
  condensed rings $\underline E$ and $\underline{\cO}_E$. Here $E$ has the topology
  restricted from $\Qlb$, and $\cO_E=\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$ is its ring of integers.

Postcomposition with continuous inclusions gives the morphisms of condensed rings
$\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$, and, when $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$ compatibly with
the embedding, $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\underline E$ and
$\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$.

proof.text: Take the point site and condensed rings to have the covering families and sheaves specified in the statement. For any topological ring $T$, [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] supplies precisely the sheaf $S\mapsto C(S,T)$ with pointwise operations and restriction by precomposition; its conclusion includes commutativity of the underlying ring object when $T$ is commutative. For an arbitrary sheaf of rings on this site, part 3 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object] supplies the claimed underlying abelian-sheaf ring object. Thus both the general convention and the continuous-map construction use the stated tensor on abelian sheaves.

source.place: First two sentences: sheaf property and ring object

proof.text: For a continuous ring homomorphism $\varphi:T\to T\prime$, apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Its component is $a\mapsto\varphi\circ a$; naturality expresses $\varphi\circ(a\circ u)=(\varphi\circ a)\circ u$. Its identity and composition clauses give exactly the asserted functoriality, with no additional condition on $T$ or $T\prime$.

For the fixed prime $\ell$, [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring] and [def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring] identify the two instances with $C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ and $C(S,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ in their $\ell$-adic topologies, and assert commutativity of their ring objects. These are the required integral and rational coefficient rings.

source.place: Four adic instances: integers and rationals

proof.text: For the given embedding $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] gives the restricted topology and $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$. With exactly that topology, [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] defines $\cO_E=\{x:|x|_E\le1\}$ with its subspace topology and gives $\underline{\cO}_E(S)=C(S,\cO_E)$. Both statements assert commutativity. Neither requires $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ to be finite.

source.place: Four adic instances: subfields and their valuation subrings

proof.text: The inclusions are the postcomposition maps stated in [def-sfb-padic-condensed-ring], [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring]. The first gives $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and the last always gives $\underline{\cO}_E\to\underline E$. Under precisely the extra compatible $\mathbf Q_\ell$-extension hypothesis of the item, the second gives $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\underline E$ and the last gives $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\cO}_E$. These are all the displayed arrows; their composites are postcomposition with the corresponding composite inclusions by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map].

source.place: Final two sentences: inclusions and commutative ring objects

The sk and det ring-object tensors agree: both are a(F⊗_pG), by clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed. Step 2: the map node gives a↦φ∘a, (id)_*=id and (ψ∘φ)_*=ψ_*∘φ_*.
